wrong.label: C = 3m + 2.5
wrong.line: The £2.50 is charged for each mile, so it goes with \(m\).

wrong.label: C = 5.5m
wrong.line: The £3 booking fee is paid once, not for each mile.

wrong.label: C = 2.5(m + 3)
wrong.line: The booking fee is not multiplied by 2.5.

worked: £2.50 for each of \(m\) miles: \(2.5m\).
Add the £3 booking fee, paid once: \(C = 2.5m + 3\).

wrong.label: T = 5x
wrong.line: That is the sand only: add the \(x\) kg of cement.

wrong.label: T = x + 5
wrong.line: The sand is 5 times the cement, not 5 more.

wrong.label: T = x + 6
wrong.line: Sand to cement is 5 : 1, so the sand is \(5x\), not 5.

worked: Sand to cement is 5 : 1, so the sand is 5 times the cement: \(5x\) kg.
Total: \(5x + x = 6x\), so \(T = 6x\).

wrong.label: T = 60h + 45
wrong.line: The £45 is charged each hour, so it goes with \(h\).

wrong.label: T = 105h
wrong.line: The £60 call-out is charged once, not each hour.

wrong.label: T = 45(h + 60)
wrong.line: The call-out charge is not multiplied by 45.

worked: £45 for each of \(h\) hours: \(45h\).
Add the £60 call-out, charged once: \(T = 45h + 60\).

wrong.label: S = 5e + 4
wrong.line: Her brother is younger, so his age is \(e - 4\).

wrong.label: S = 4e - 4
wrong.line: That leaves out Ellie's own age, \(e\).

wrong.label: S = 4e
wrong.line: That leaves out her brother, \(e - 4\).

worked: Ellie: \(e\). Her brother: \(e - 4\). Their mum: \(3e\).
Add them: \(S = e + (e - 4) + 3e = 5e - 4\).

wrong.label: N = 24x + 6
wrong.line: The 6 packets are kept aside, so take them away.

wrong.label: N = 18x
wrong.line: The 6 packets are taken from the whole order once, not from every box.

wrong.label: N = 24(x - 6)
wrong.line: That keeps back 6 boxes, not 6 packets.

worked: Each box holds 24 packets: \(x\) boxes hold \(24x\).
Take away the 6 kept aside: \(N = 24x - 6\).
QUESTIONS[10].stem_override: Packets of crisps come in boxes of 24. A café orders \(x\) boxes and keeps 6 packets aside as samples. Write a formula for the number of packets, \(N\), available to sell.

wrong.label: \frac{8V}{3} = 360
wrong.line: Three-eighths means \(\frac{3}{8}\) of \(V\): 3 on top, 8 underneath.

wrong.label: 3V = 360
wrong.line: Three-eighths of \(V\) is \(3V\) divided by 8.

wrong.label: V - \frac{3}{8} = 360
wrong.line: "Three-eighths full" means \(\frac{3}{8}\) of \(V\), not \(V\) take away \(\frac{3}{8}\).

worked: Three-eighths of the full amount \(V\) is \(\frac{3V}{8}\).
That amount is 360 litres: \(\frac{3V}{8} = 360\).

wrong.label: h = \frac{T + 60}{45}
wrong.line: The £60 call-out is part of \(T\), so take it away.

wrong.label: h = \frac{T}{45} - 60
wrong.line: Take away the £60 before dividing by 45.

wrong.label: h = 45(T - 60)
wrong.line: To find the hours, divide by the £45 an hour.

worked: The charge is \(T = 45h + 60\).
Take the £60 call-out away: \(T - 60 = 45h\).
Divide by 45: \(h = \frac{T - 60}{45}\).

wrong.label: 2n + 9 = 25
wrong.line: 9 is subtracted, so it is \(- 9\).

wrong.label: 2(n - 9) = 25
wrong.line: The number is doubled first, then 9 is subtracted.

wrong.label: n^2 - 9 = 25
wrong.line: Doubled means times 2, not squared.

worked: Doubled: \(2n\).
Then subtract 9: \(2n - 9\).
That gives 25: \(2n - 9 = 25\).

wrong.label: \frac{8V}{3} = 360
wrong.line: Three-eighths means \(\frac{3}{8}\) of \(V\): 3 on top, 8 underneath.

wrong.label: 3V = 360
wrong.line: Three-eighths of \(V\) is \(3V\) divided by 8.

wrong.label: V - \frac{3}{8} = 360
wrong.line: "Three-eighths full" means \(\frac{3}{8}\) of \(V\), not \(V\) take away \(\frac{3}{8}\).

worked: Three-eighths of the full capacity \(V\) is \(\frac{3V}{8}\).
That amount is 360 litres: \(\frac{3V}{8} = 360\).

probability_stage1.rule: choice: the answer word plus the three other words nearest it on the scale (drop the one furthest away); no slip lines.

worked: Breathing today must happen.
Something that must happen is certain.
The faces of a standard die are 1 to 6, so a 7 cannot happen.
Something that cannot happen is impossible.
Rain somewhere in Britain in a week happens far more often than not.
It is not guaranteed, so it is likely, not certain.
A fair coin has 2 equally likely outcomes, and heads is 1 of them.
1 out of 2 is an even chance.
January, June and July start with J: 3 of the 12 months.
3 out of 12 is less than half, so it is unlikely.
Half the cards in a standard pack are red: 26 of 52.
Half is an even chance.
2, 4 and 6 are even: 3 of the 6 faces.
3 out of 6 is a half, an even chance.
One ticket has about a 1 in 45 million chance of winning.
It could happen, so it is not impossible, but it is very unlikely.
Boys and girls are born in very nearly equal numbers.
So it is about an even chance.
The sun rises every day.
So it is certain.
